cost.question: Does it cost anything?
cost.answer: No. TradeIQ is free to use.

account.question: Do I need an account?
account.answer: Not to look up companies or test an idea. You need one to save a test or to practise with virtual money.

advice.question: Will TradeIQ tell me what to buy?
advice.answer: No. TradeIQ is for learning and trying ideas. It doesn’t give investment advice.

whatBacktest.question: What is backtesting?
whatBacktest.answer: Trying a buying and selling rule on past prices to see how it would have done.

rules.question: What rules can I use?
rules.answer: Buy on the first day, after the price falls by a set percentage, or when it drops to a set price. Sell at a profit target, a loss limit, a set price, or at the end of the period.

backtestFees.question: Are fees included?
backtestFees.answer: Yes. Each buy and sell pays standard CSE fees of 1.12%. You can change them in the Advanced setup.

save.question: Is my test saved?
save.answer: Only if you have an account. Otherwise the result stays in your browser tab until you close it.

future.question: If a rule worked before, will it work again?
future.answer: Not necessarily. Past results don’t promise future ones.

manyCompanies.question: Can I test more than one company at once?
manyCompanies.answer: Not yet. Each test uses one company.

whatPaper.question: What is paper trading?
whatPaper.answer: Buying and selling shares with virtual money, so you can practise without risk.

virtualMoney.question: How much virtual money do I get?
virtualMoney.answer: Rs. 1,000,000 to start. You can pick any amount from Rs. 100,000 to Rs. 100,000,000.

price.question: What price do I pay?
price.answer: The latest closing price. On weekends and holidays, that’s the close from the last trading day.

fill.question: When does my order go through?
fill.answer: Straight away. The whole order goes through, or none of it does.

paperFees.question: Do I pay fees?
paperFees.answer: Yes, 1.12% on each buy and sell, based on standard CSE fees. It comes out of your virtual cash.

cantTrade.question: Why can’t I trade some companies?
cantTrade.answer: Suspended or delisted companies can’t be traded. Neither can a company with no price for the latest trading day.

source.question: Where do the prices come from?
source.answer: Public data from the Colombo Stock Exchange.

fresh.question: How up to date are the prices?
fresh.answer: They’re closing prices, updated once a day after the market closes.

history.question: How far back does the data go?

gaps.question: Why are some parts of a chart grey?
gaps.answer: Those are data gaps, days where prices are missing. TradeIQ never fills them with guesses. The Markets page lists every gap.

apiReference.title: API reference
apiReference.intro: Read-only Colombo Stock Exchange data for your application. Explore six resources, request examples, and the shapes of successful and error responses.
apiReference.authMore: Create a key after signing in. One key can be active per account, and its full secret is shown only when created or regenerated. Keep it out of URLs, committed source, and public client code. Revocation may take up to 60 seconds to take effect across all requests. The interactive explorer keeps authorization in memory only; Execute sends a real request and uses your quota.
apiReference.edgeLimit: A separate per-IP rate limit can also return 429 with Retry-After. That response may omit reset_at and per-key quota headers. Requests can still succeed when X-RateLimit-Remaining is unavailable; treat a missing count as unknown.
apiReference.dates: Date filters use valid YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates, include both boundaries, and require from ≤ to. End dates default to the latest available session; start dates default to one calendar year earlier. For index history, the default end date is the latest observation across all indices. Defaults depend on stored coverage.
apiReference.paginateNote: Every request uses quota. This Python example stops when meta.total is reached or an empty page is returned; a 429 raises an error so you can wait until the reset rather than retry continuously.
apiReference.aggregateNote: Daily bars have date; weekly and monthly bars have period_start and period_end. Aggregates only include daily observations inside your requested range, so boundary periods may be partial. Open is the earliest non-null opening price in that period. Series are ascending, gaps are not filled, and index history contains close values only.
apiReference.generatedNote: Endpoint descriptions and field definitions are available in English; guides and navigation follow your selected language.
apiReference.name: Name
apiReference.noParameters: No path or query parameters. The X-API-Key header is still required.
apiReference.illustrative: Example response. Actual values and available dates may differ.
apiReference.errorHandling: 401 means the key was not accepted. 400 includes fields describing invalid inputs. 404 identifies an unknown security or index. For 429, honor Retry-After and inspect reset_at when present. Keep trace_id when reporting an error. An empty successful result is different from an unknown identifier.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: The canonical base URL below exposes GET resources for security descriptions, historical prices, indices, and exact-session end-of-day data. No trading or account operations are exposed. This is historical and latest available end-of-day data; there are no intraday quotes or guaranteed publication times. Documentation and the OpenAPI specification are public, key-free, and uncounted.

authentication.title: Authentication and keys
authentication.body: Send an active key in the X-API-Key header on every data request. A key has the form tiq_ followed by 40 letters and digits. Keys in URL query parameters and website sign-in tokens are not accepted. Missing, malformed, unknown, and revoked keys share the same 401 UNAUTHENTICATED response. Public resources allow cross-origin GET requests and key-free, uncounted OPTIONS preflight.

rate-limits.title: Rate limits
rate-limits.body: The default allowance is 100 requests per active key per UTC clock hour. It resets at the next hour, rather than one hour after your first request. The configured allowance can differ: response headers are authoritative. Requests accepted for an active key count even when they return validation or not-found errors. Authentication failures before key resolution do not use that key’s quota. On a per-key 429, Retry-After gives seconds until reset and error.reset_at gives its UTC timestamp.

pagination.title: Pagination and dates
pagination.body: Paginated resources accept page (minimum and default 1) and page_size, with each operation’s default and maximum below. meta.total counts all matching rows or bars, not just the current page. Pages beyond the result set return 200 and an empty array. Security lists and EOD are ordered by symbol; index lists by code; histories by ascending date or period.

data-conventions.title: Data conventions
data-conventions.body: Symbols and index codes match case-insensitively and responses use canonical forms. Prices and changes are JSON numbers; volumes and share counts are integers. Percentages use percentage units: 0.47 means 0.47%. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD and timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC. A null value means unavailable, not zero. Use security symbols and index codes to identify resources.

errors.title: Errors
errors.body: Errors use an error object containing code, message, and trace_id. Validation errors add fields; the per-key quota error adds reset_at. Each operation lists its applicable statuses below, and the response schemas include these envelopes. Per-IP rate-limit errors may omit reset_at and per-key quota headers. Check the HTTP status before using data.

versioning.title: Versioning
versioning.body: v1 changes are additive. Breaking changes require a separate v2 running alongside v1. Clients should tolerate additional response fields.

securities.title: List securities
securities.note: Returns descriptive attributes without current prices. Search matches a symbol prefix or company-name substring, ignoring case; % and _ are literal characters. Search must contain 1–100 characters. Sector must be a known GICS code. Listings can be listed, suspended, or delisted, and price coverage can be unavailable.

security.title: Get a security
security.note: Look up one security by symbol, using 1–20 characters. An unknown symbol returns 404; a known security without price history still has a descriptive record, with nullable coverage dates. There is no pagination on this operation.

ohlcv.title: Security OHLCV
ohlcv.note: Returns daily (default), weekly, or monthly bars for a security. The example asks for daily observations in an explicit historical range. Empty ranges return 200 with bars: [] and meta.total: 0. Opening prices can be null for any session. See data conventions for aggregate boundaries and missing sessions.

indices.title: List indices
indices.note: Returns index descriptions and their own latest available observations, which can have different dates. Supported codes include ASPI, ASTRI, SL20, and SL20TRI. Changes compare with the previous available point, even across gaps. latest is null when an index has no observations.

values.title: Index history
values.note: Returns daily close values for one exact index code, matched without case sensitivity. SL20 and SL20TRI identify different series. Empty ranges return 200 with values: [] and meta.total: 0. Missing dates are not forward-filled; this endpoint does not expose index OHLCV.

eod.title: End-of-day data
eod.note: Returns one session’s security OHLCV and changes, sorted by symbol. date defaults to the latest completed session. An explicit date without data, such as a weekend or holiday, returns 200 with data: [], meta.total: 0, and meta.as_of: null. It does not fall back to the previous session.

setup.availableOnly: These are saved model setups. Changing a choice loads an existing result; it does not run a new test.

result.title: Model estimate
result.help: This is the model’s estimated probability of reaching the profit target before the loss threshold within the trading period. It is not measured accuracy or a guaranteed outcome.
result.question: From the closing price on {{date}}, the model estimates the chance of reaching a {{target}} gain before a {{loss}} fall, within {{count}} trading days.
result.signalMeaning: This setup meets the model’s condition for a long trade. It does not place an order.
result.noSignalMeaning: This setup does not meet the model’s condition for a long trade. This does not mean you should sell or that the price will fall.
result.older: Company prices are available through {{date}}. The estimate above still uses its own displayed data date.
result.caution: The estimate can be wrong. It is not a guaranteed return or a buy or sell instruction.
result.reference: The setup starts from the closing price on the data date shown above. Its trading period also starts from that date, rather than the time you open this page.
